title: Danish residence and work permit under the Pay Limit Scheme: a job offer with annual pay of at least DKK 552,000 (2026)

sources.title: Aliens Act (consolidated Act No. 953 of 2026), § 9 a(2)(3) and (29): a job offer with annual pay of at least DKK 400,000, adjusted each year in line with wage growth and rounded to DKK 1,000
SIRI, the Pay Limit Scheme: the pay limit is DKK 552,000 a year for 2026, set each 1 January; only cash pay, pension and paid holiday allowance count; pay and terms usual in Denmark
Aliens Act, § 9 a(9), (10), (25) and (26): at least 30 hours a week; pay into a Danish bank account; no permit for a job in a lawful labour dispute or for an offer that is not genuine
Aliens Act, § 9 a(4): the permit requires that the principal and the family members who get permits through them receive no assistance under the Active Social Policy Act
Aliens Act, § 9 m(1): where essential business or employment interests favour it, a family member of a foreigner with a § 9 a(2) permit may get one, if they share a home
SIRI, accompanying family of employees: a spouse or registered partner, a cohabiting partner over 18 after at least 1.5 to 2 years living together, and a child under 18
Aliens Act, §§ 1 and 2: citizens of Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden live in Denmark without a permit; EU and EEA citizens fall under the EU rules on free movement
EU Residence Order (Order No. 1457 of 2020), §§ 1(2) and 2(2): Swiss citizens are treated like EU citizens under the EU rules on free movement
Guardianship Act (Act No. 1122 of 2021), § 1: under-18s who have not married are minors; no Danish rule for a 29 February birthday was found, so 28 February is assumed

requirements.title: Not a citizen of Denmark, another Nordic country, an EU or EEA state or Switzerland: they live and work in Denmark without this permit

assessments.title: A job offer in Denmark with annual pay of at least the pay limit: DKK 400,000 in the act, adjusted each year for wage growth; DKK 552,000 for 2026 as SIRI publishes it
At least 30 hours a week; pay and terms usual for the field in Denmark; pay into a Danish bank account opened within 180 days; a genuine offer; no lawful labour dispute
Family members share the principal's home, and while the permits last none of them, the principal included, receives social assistance under the Active Social Policy Act

dependents.title: Spouse who was 18 or more at the wedding; married younger, both now 18 or more: possible, as a cohabiting partner after at least 1.5 to 2 years living together
Partner, both aged 18 or more: after 2 years together; a shorter union, which may be a registered partnership: possible
